meta.title: Partners in Literacy Haiti

problem.title: We visited 32 classrooms and found zero books.
problem.body: Not one storybook. Not one bookshelf. Across six rural schools and thirty two classrooms, children had nothing to read beyond their required lessons, and no chance to discover the joy of reading for themselves. For families struggling to meet basic needs, buying books is out of reach, and rural schools face the same hard choices. Your support helps change that, one book, one classroom, and one young reader at a time.

approach.title: Three things, done properly, in one village at a time.
approach.lede: We do not parachute in. We partner with a village that wants a library, and we stay for years.

items.title: Books in Kreyòl

involved.title: This work runs on people who remember where they come from.
involved.lede: PILH is an all volunteer organization with roots in Haiti and hands around the world. Wherever you live, there is a seat for you.
involved.diasporaBody: You left, but Haiti never left you. From Miami, Brooklyn, Montreal, Boston, Paris or Santiago, you can put Kreyòl books into the hands of children in the village your family calls home. Sponsor a library, fund a monthly book shipment, translate a story, or lend your professional skills for a few hours a month. Every committee meets on Zoom, in the language you prefer.

aboutPage.title: Reading is the bridge to equity.
aboutPage.lede: One vision, one mission, five values. This is the whole playbook.
aboutPage.vision: Partners in Literacy Haiti collaborates with the Haitian people, libraries and educational institutions so that reading proficiency and learning success rise together.
aboutPage.mission: Enhance reading through Kreyòl books, technology and training for children from birth to eight years old, their families and their teachers, in community libraries, schools and centers.

values.title: Partnership
values.body: We partner with organizations that share our vision. Never alone, never around the community.

values.title: Action
values.body: As many children as possible, as early as possible. The first years are when a brain builds itself.

values.title: Education
values.body: Passion for learning, with the flexibility to find new solutions when old ones stop working.

values.title: Stewardship
values.body: Every dollar is used responsibly. Our board is entirely volunteer.

values.title: Literacy equality
values.body: We raise the reading ability of the most marginalized children first, not last.

aboutPage.sdgTitle: Part of the United Nations 2030 agenda
aboutPage.sdgBody: The UN names libraries as key partners in its seventeen Sustainable Development Goals, because a library gives a community access to information, protects cultural heritage and puts knowledge in people's hands. Every PILH village library advances that agenda.
aboutPage.openTitle: This work is open to you
aboutPage.openBody: Involvement with PILH is open to anyone who wants to help young children become readers and who embraces this vision, mission and these values.

historyPage.title: Fifteen years, one page at a time.
historyPage.lede: From an epiphany in a mountain village to a national policy change. Scroll the story.

epiphany.title: An epiphany at Cange
epiphany.body: At a Rotary leaders meeting in Haiti, Dr. Sara Mansbach visits villages where children have never seen a picture book. She finds a new life purpose.

rotary.title: The volunteer years begin
rotary.body: An all volunteer Rotary Charities committee starts developing village libraries in the Central Plateau and the Artibonite. Over the next decade it donates more than 5,000 French and Kreyòl books and trains teachers and library workers.

materials.title: Making our own books
materials.body: With an Australian Rotary club and a Haitian team of illustrators and translators, six Kreyòl easy readers are co published. The Alfabè Kreyòl Mwen alphabet chart, thirteen years in the making with MIT linguists, reaches 98 schools, 95 teachers and 3,800 students.

nonprofit.title: PILH becomes independent
nonprofit.body: Federal 501(c)(3) status arrives, EIN 87-0904773. Independence brings talented people, a paid Haitian consultant, and real fundraising for a growing waiting list of villages.

duplan.title: The Duplan project launches
duplan.body: At the village's request, PILH begins modernizing the twenty year old Methodist Community Library: a Kreyòl collection, six new Chromebooks, and an eleven module training curriculum led by Erick Toussaint.

kreyol.title: Kreyòl becomes the language of the classroom
kreyol.body: Haiti's Ministry of Education decrees that children learn in Kreyòl, the mother tongue. The premise PILH built on for a decade becomes national policy.

books.title: Three thousand books and counting
books.body: Over 3,000 PILH Kreyòl books are now in children's hands across rural Haiti, and the model keeps scaling: five libraries mentored, a waiting list of villages, and a generation learning to love reading in its own language.

historyPage.todayBody: A training center at Duplan that educates library workers for the whole country. More villages off the waiting list. You are welcome to write the next chapter with us.

duplanPage.title: Duplan: a village library reborn.
duplanPage.lede: A twenty year old library in the Ouest, rebuilt as a modern children's library and a future training center for the whole country.

duplanPage.whyBody: Central in the country, semi rural and relatively secure, with a school unique in the region and great potential for service. Pastor Edzaire Paul founded the library more than twenty years ago and champions its modernization. A signed agreement between PILH and the village governance committee frames the whole project.

kreyolPage.title: Books written for Haitian children, in their own language.
kreyolPage.lede: Six easy readers and an alphabet chart thirteen years in the making. Every page edited by Haitian linguists.
kreyolPage.whyBody: Our field research found rural classrooms with no books and no alphabet charts at all. So we found partners and made them ourselves. Teacher workshops around these materials drew overflow crowds, and independent evaluations came back asking for more.

kreyolPage.chartTitle: Alfabè Kreyòl Mwen, the alphabet chart
kreyolPage.chartBody: Kreyòl blends Taino, French, African languages, English, Portuguese and Spanish, so it holds more sounds than most alphabets. This chart took thirteen years of classroom testing, was verified by Professor Michel DeGraff of the MIT Haiti Initiative, and is registered with the US Library of Congress.
chartFacts: Waterproof vinyl, made for the tropics
kreyolPage.pricingNote: Books ship from Haiti, so delays are possible. Charts ship from the USA. Reselling and reprinting are not permitted.
kreyolPage.orderBody: Send us your name, email, where the materials will be used, a postal code, and the items and quantities you want. We reply with shipping cost and delivery time.
kreyolPage.inventoryBody: Our printed book inventory is fully depleted, and about 50 alphabet charts remain. New donations fund the next print run, shipping, and electronic distribution of these materials. Chart orders ship while supplies last, and book orders join a waiting list for the next printing.

workPage.startTitle: Start a library in your village
workPage.startBody: A children's library begins with a village that wants one and will invest in it. Apply, join a Zoom or WhatsApp interview, and our review committee selects. The village commits to four things:
commitments: Pay the library worker. We help you interview an enthusiastic candidate.
Maintain strong wi-fi for training sessions and village meetings.
Elect an active library committee of teachers and village leaders.
Develop realistic, workable ideas for sustainability.
workPage.waitNote: As a young nonprofit we keep a waiting list for service. That list is exactly why your support matters.
workPage.wordsBody: In Haiti, a library worker runs a library without formal certification, because the country has no accrediting program. A librarian holds a degree in library science. Haiti has only a few handfuls of certified librarians for eleven and a half million people. Changing that is part of our long game.

librariesPage.title: A culture of children's libraries, built village by village.
librariesPage.lede: We strengthen rural libraries until they stand on their own. Here is the standard we mentor toward, and the five libraries living it.

readersPage.title: The reader is built before the fifth birthday.
readersPage.lede: Haiti's future depends on a generation that reads. The window opens at birth, and it opens in Kreyòl.
readersPage.windowBody: A child's brain builds itself most intensively from birth to age four. Libraries equip village teachers, parents and caregivers with that knowledge, and with the books that turn it into daily practice. The joy has to come first, and it has to come in Kreyòl, with books that teach, delight and challenge.

desertLabels.books: extra books we found in them

readersPage.desertBody: Not one bookshelf, and no source of books anywhere nearby. Haiti's mountain villages are cut off from age appropriate books and from a culture of reading. Seventy percent of primary schools are private and rarely budget for pleasure reading. Where a family lives on less than 2.15 dollars a day, buying books is out of reach. A library or book corner nearby changes the paradigm.
readersPage.whyBody: Kreyòl is the spoken language of ninety five percent of Haiti's people. The old standard was colonial French, taught by rote, which frustrated struggling readers. UNESCO's education institute reports that about forty percent of Haitian children leave school before ninth grade.
readersPage.policyCallout: In February 2022 Haiti's Minister of Education proclaimed that public schools should teach children aged three to eight in Kreyòl. Every PILH book, chart and training is built on the premise the government now shares: a Haitian child should learn to read in the Haitian language.
readersPage.ctaTitle: Put ten books in young hands
readersPage.ctaBody: Fifteen dollars a month funds ten Kreyòl children's books, every month.

alliancePage.title: The Haiti Libraries Alliance
alliancePage.lede: A free community of library workers and library advocates, inside Haiti and around the world.
alliancePage.aboutBody: The Alliance promotes libraries, strengthens librarianship and connects library people through information sharing, capacity development and collaboration. It was established in 2020 after a survey of Haiti's libraries and stakeholders, and began monthly meetings and its e-list in 2021. It is a collaboration between the Mortenson Center for International Library Programs at the University of Illinois and Partners in Literacy Haiti.

numbersPage.title: The evidence behind every decision.
numbersPage.lede: We work from data, not sentiment. Here is the context that shapes our strategy, from sources you can check.

contextStats.label: people, with Kreyòl and French as official languages
speak Kreyòl. At most one in ten speaks French
live in poverty, most on subsistence farming
a day is the minimum wage, and two thirds lack formal jobs

numbersPage.chartNote: Percent scale, 0 to 100. Source: USAID International Data and Economic Analysis, November 2022. Regional figures are Latin America and the Caribbean.

indicators.outOfSchool: Children out of school, % of primary age

numbersPage.takeBody: Two numbers drive our strategy. Ninety five percent of Haitians speak Kreyòl, and pre primary enrollment sits near five percent. The earliest learners are the least served, in the language almost nobody prints books in. That is exactly where a children's library changes lives, and exactly where PILH works.
numbersPage.sourceNote: Recent years of unrest, Covid and the 2021 Grand Sud earthquake kept many schools closed or late to open, so current conditions are likely harder than these figures show.
numbersPage.contextSources: Sources: CIA World Factbook. USAID International Data and Economic Analysis, November 2022.
